extraction_notes: PDF SHA-256 matches the expected hash 638e5dc21198745acc0f6e832f464119c245f142a8156a4e01b662a44acab421.
The forward and reverse curves were digitized from the actual vector plots on p. 2; no interpolated points were added.
Fig. 3 is a typical forward-bias curve at Tj = 25 degC, pulse width = 300 us, and 1% duty cycle, with logarithmic current axis.
Fig. 4 uses percent of rated peak reverse voltage on the x-axis. For M7F, VRRM is 1000 V. Separate Tj = 25 degC and Tj = 125 degC reverse-bias curves are retained.
The tabulated forward-voltage point is a maximum value of 1.0 V at IF = 1.0 A, not a typical value.
The tabulated reverse-current point is a maximum value of 2.0 uA at VR = VDC = 1000 V and TA = 25 degC.
The tabulated junction capacitance is typical, 15 pF at 4.0 V DC and 1 MHz.
Reverse recovery is not modelled: the datasheet publishes no reverse-recovery time.
Reverse breakdown is not modelled: the datasheet publishes no breakdown-voltage or breakdown-current characteristic.
No self-heating: junction temperature is fixed at the stated test conditions. Thermal derating from the datasheet is not modelled.
Package parasitics such as lead inductance and package capacitance are not modelled.
